artifacts.name: Hot-spots & cold-spots
artifacts.summary: Global Moran’s I = -0.40. 0 hot-spot and 0 cold-spot neighbourhood(s) of drinking water points density (local Moran’s I / LISA). Only 10 sub-areas: too few for the permutation test to establish significance, so read a grey map as "not enough units to tell", not as "no clustering". Use a finer `subarea_mode` or a larger area to make this map informative. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Sub-areas classified by the local Moran’s I statistic (LISA) over drinking water points density: **High-High** = a dense neighbourhood surrounded by others like it (hot-spot); **Low-Low** = a sparse one among others like it (cold-spot); **High-Low / Low-High** = spatial outliers. Significance uses a deterministic permutation test; non-significant sub-areas are greyed out.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: drinking_water · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Hot-spots & cold-spots (per capita)
artifacts.summary: Global Moran’s I = -0.29. 0 hot-spot and 0 cold-spot neighbourhood(s) of drinking water points per 1,000 residents (local Moran’s I / LISA). Only 10 sub-areas: too few for the permutation test to establish significance, so read a grey map as "not enough units to tell", not as "no clustering". Use a finer `subarea_mode` or a larger area to make this map informative. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Sub-areas classified by the local Moran’s I statistic (LISA) over drinking water points per 1,000 residents: **High-High** = a well-supplied neighbourhood surrounded by others like it (hot-spot); **Low-Low** = a poorly-supplied one among others like it (cold-spot); **High-Low / Low-High** = spatial outliers. Significance uses a deterministic permutation test; non-significant sub-areas are greyed out.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: drinking_water · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Any drinking-water source
artifacts.summary: A combined layer (max) of 1×Drinking water points, 1×Water taps & filling points, 1×Drinking fountains, 1×Potable springs, per sub-area. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Map algebra: for each administrative sub-area, the per-km² densities of the input categories are combined by **max** — 1×Drinking water points, 1×Water taps & filling points, 1×Drinking fountains, 1×Potable springs — into a single value. Use it to express a composite index (e.g. a weighted suitability score) as one layer instead of several.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: drinking_water · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Unserved residents
artifacts.summary: A combined layer (weighted sum) of 1×population, -1×per 1000 inhabitants, per sub-area. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Map algebra: for each administrative sub-area, the normalised densities of the input categories are combined by **weighted sum** — 1×population, -1×per 1000 inhabitants — into a single value. Each category is first rescaled to 0–1 across sub-areas, so the value is a unitless index. Use it to express a composite index (e.g. a weighted suitability score) as one layer instead of several.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: drinking_water · reachability: straight-line distance.

Each administrative sub-area shaded by its number of drinking water points per 1,000 inhabitants, so the colour reflects provision *relative to residents* rather than raw density. A populous sub-area with average density can still read as under-served here. Sub-areas without usable population data are omitted.
